reasons: The cited clause gives Licensor a unilateral option to extend a 36-month initial term by seven years, with no Licensee opt-out and no uplift cap — an automatic/vendor-elected multi-year renewal that sits in the rule's walk-away band and fails the fallback (≤60-day notice window, uplift ≤5%), so 'deviation' is correctly classified rather than an acceptable fallback.

The redline is targeted (it replaces only the offending renewal sentence) and reaches the preferred position: successive 12-month terms, a 30-day non-renewal right exercisable by either party, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. The failed 'notice window ≤ 60 days' regex is a phrasing artifact — 'thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current period' is present — and the 0.782 changed-character ratio reflects a rule-mandated rewrite of the renewal mechanic.
Comment is concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and the specific objection (seven-year Licensor-option extension); tone and prefix conform.

Minor, non-fatal: the new automatic-renewal mechanic sits somewhat awkwardly beside Article IV(II)-(III), which require extension by mutual written agreement, so the comment's assertion that the edit is 'consistent with' those subsections overstates matters. If a cleaner conform is wanted, simply deleting the Licensor-option sentence would leave the mutual-agreement mechanic intact and be an even smaller edit; consider noting that as the alternative in negotiation.
